01

Meet Telex Cues

Bring prose, notes or an existing script. Telex Cues adds navigable section headings while preserving your wording and language by default. Ask for a rewrite when you want notes expanded into a spoken script.

This is a separate skill for Codex. It does not install AI inside Telex, transcribe your voice or change app settings.

View the MIT-licensed skill on GitHub ↗
02

Install in Codex

Ask Codex’s skill installer:

Use $skill-installer to install the skill at the root of
https://github.com/ishuu9837/telex-cues with the name telex-cues.

Or clone it into your personal skills directory if that destination does not already exist:

git clone https://github.com/ishuu9837/telex-cues.git ~/.codex/skills/telex-cues

The skill is available on your next Codex turn after installation. If you already have a local copy, review it before updating so custom edits are preserved.

03

Prepare your script

Use $telex-cues to prepare this text for Telex.
Keep my wording and language. Add short section cues.
Save the result as a UTF-8 .txt file.

[paste your text here]

Copy the result into the editor, or use Import script in Telex. Review your script before reading. The skill does not automatically import, start playback or overwrite an existing script.

04

Small cues. Clear sections.

# Opening
Welcome, everyone.
Today we review our progress.

# Next steps
Next, we will gather feedback.

Each heading sits on its own line with a normal space after #. You can also use [Cue: Next steps] on its own line. Titles remain visible in the prompter. Labels such as [pause] or [speed: 90] are ordinary text, not playback commands.

The skill keeps names, numbers and claims intact unless you request rewriting. It does not invent supporting facts. Long content should be split into scripts within Telex’s 500,000-character limit.

05

Keep the boundaries clear

The skill contains no networking or capture code and does not require microphone, camera, Speech or screen-recording permissions. However, text you supply to Codex is processed under your Codex service and account settings. Telex’s local script storage does not make AI preparation on-device.

Use content you are comfortable providing to Codex. App permission choices, playback and sharing remain separate actions under your control.
